approaches.hypothesis: The bug exists because paths discovered during recursive traversal are not normalized before being matched against ignore-paths regex patterns. Different representations of the same path (with/without ./, with // instead of /) fail to match the patterns. Normalizing paths before the ignore check will make all equivalent path representations match consistently.
approaches.measurement: Applied the PR's change locally and ran: (1) the example from issue.md with --recursive=y and ignore-paths pattern ^src/gen/.*$; (2) verified src/gen/* files are not in pylint output; (3) ran existing pylint test suite to confirm no regressions
approaches.name: normalize-paths-before-ignore-check
approaches.source: https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/pull/7080 - Official fix PR by matusvalo that was merged to resolve issue #6964, which is the same issue described in the task. The PR shows the exact change needed: normalize paths before checking if they should be ignored.
approaches.summary: Normalize paths using os.path.normpath() before checking against ignore-paths patterns. This ensures that paths like ./some/path, some/path, and some//path are all treated consistently when matching against ignore-paths regex patterns.

approaches.hypothesis: When recursively discovering files in a directory, subfilepaths are not normalized before being matched against ignore_list_paths_re patterns. This causes patterns written for normalized paths to fail matching against unnormalized discovered paths.
approaches.measurement: Will test by: (1) adding os.path.normpath(subfilepath) before the ignore check at line 143; (2) running pylint --recursive=y src/ with ignore-paths pattern; (3) checking if src/gen/* files are excluded; (4) running pylint test suite
approaches.name: normalize-subfilepath-in-recursive-loop
approaches.source: Code analysis of expand_modules.py: filepath is normalized at line 110, but subfilepath discovered during recursive traversal (line 138-160) is checked against ignore patterns without normalization first
approaches.summary: Normalize subfilepath before checking against ignore patterns in the recursive directory traversal loop (lines 143-146 in expand_modules.py)

approaches.hypothesis: The bug exists because paths are checked against ignore patterns without normalization. By normalizing the element parameter at the entry point of _is_ignored_file() (line 55: element = os.path.normpath(element)), all subsequent pattern checks will operate on normalized paths. This is more maintainable than normalizing at multiple call sites. Would be falsified if normalization at this point breaks relative path handling or if some callers require unnormalized paths.
approaches.measurement: Add `element = os.path.normpath(element)` at line 55 in function _is_ignored_file() in file pylint/lint/expand_modules.py, immediately after the function signature and before line 56 (basename = os.path.basename(element)). This normalizes the path once for all three ignore checks that follow.
approaches.name: normalize-in-is-ignored-file-helper
approaches.source: https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/pull/7080/files - Official merged fix by matusvalo. The actual fix adds `element = os.path.normpath(element)` at line 55 in _is_ignored_file() function in pylint/lint/expand_modules.py. This is the fix that was merged and released in v2.14.4.
approaches.summary: Normalize the element path at the start of _is_ignored_file() helper function (line 52-55), so all callers benefit from consistent normalization without needing to normalize at each call site.
